content: Potiguar University, known in Portuguese as Universidade Potiguar (UnP), is a private institution located in Natal, Brazil. It provides a wide range of degree programs, including those in technology, law, environmental studies, architecture, tourism, social work, arts, and sciences. Established in 1981, it holds the distinction of being the first private university in the state of Rio Grande do Norte, Brazil. The university operates across two cities in the northeastern region of Brazil, Natal and Mossoró, and is organized into seven academic faculties. With a student body exceeding 32,600 individuals, it is one of the largest higher education institutions in the region. Notably, its School of Health Sciences is recognized as one of the most advanced in Latin America. Additionally, its online and distance learning programs, as well as its health sciences curriculum, are highly regarded. The university is divided into seven distinct faculties, which include the Faculty of Business and Management, the Faculty of Communication and Arts, the Faculty of Culinary Arts, the Faculty of Education, the Faculty of Engineering and Information Technology, the Faculty of Health Sciences, and the Faculty of Law. Potiguar University operates multiple campuses across the cities of Natal and Mossoró. In Natal, the campuses include Unidade Floriano Peixoto, Unidade Nascimento de Castro, Unidade Roberto Freire, and Unidade Salgado Filho. In Mossoró, the campus is known as Unidade Mossoró. The university is deeply committed to social responsibility and actively engages with the local community through various initiatives. These include health clinics that provide care to thousands of outpatients annually, legal aid services, digital education programs, and formal educational projects aimed at supporting individuals from low socioeconomic backgrounds. Additionally, the university undertakes business and entrepreneurship initiatives and implements projects that address environmental and sustainability concerns.
